newsitem.title: USA: Hutchinson Tech shrs up after higher EPS forecast.
newsitem.headline: Hutchinson Tech shrs up after higher EPS forecast.

text.p: Shares of Hutchinson Technology Inc surged on Tuesday after the company forecast first quarter earnings far above analysts' estimates.
Shares of the high-technology company, which makes suspension assemblies for computer disk drives, was up 20-3/4 at one point on Tuesday to a new peak for the year of 73-1/2.
The stock closed at 72-1/4, up 19-1/2 on volume of 2.6 million.
Early on Tuesday, Minnesota-based Hutchinson said it looked for fiscal first quarter 1997 net sales of between $104 million and $109 million.
It said it expected earnings at between $1.50 and $1.90 per share. This compares to $0.51 a share year-ago after a $0.69 per share charge.
The First Call consensus estimate is $0.71 a share.
In November, Hutchinson reported net income of $0.25 a share for the fourth quarter 1996, down from $1.55 during the same fiscal 1995 period.
The company expects to report results for the fiscal 1997 first quarter, ending December 29, on January 20, 1997.

Wayne Fortun, Hutchinson's chief executive officer, tied the improved sales and earnings outlook to better demand during the first half of the first quarter, compared to the decline seen during the fiscal 1996 fourth quarter.
"Demand has been strong for all suspension types and the manufacturing capacity we added over the last year has enabled us to keep pace with customer requirements," he said in Tuesday's news release.
After that announcement, at least two securities analysts raised their earnings forecasts to reflect the company's improved expectations.
They tied the stronger outlook to heightened demand for computers and components heading into the holiday season and the company's ability to respond.

"I think they are a little bit surprised...by how strong demand has been," said Paul Fox, analyst with Montgomery Securities. "Their execution had been really good, too...being able to meet" the strong demand.
Fox raised his first quarter earnings estimate to $1.78 a share from $0.67 and hiked his fiscal 1997 estimate to $6 a share from $3.10.
Cody Acree, analyst at Olde Discount Corp, said he raised his first quarter earnings forecast to $1.70 per share from $0.75.
He estimated that the company's weekly shipping rate had risen into the low- to mid-12-million units range per week, up from roughly 11.9 million units a week about a month ago.
But neither analyst was certain the heightened demand would last.
In fact, Fox said he looked for the March quarter to show a decline in earnings, to $1.30, with the third quarter at $1.35 and the fourth quarter bringing in $1.57 per share.
"We're not altering forward quarterly estimates...at this point," added Acree.
Fox, who said he talked with Hutchinson executives on Tuesday, said he also doubted the company is expecting the current holiday-assisted strength to continue unabated.
"They (company) don't know exactly where demand is going to be in the March quarter...." he said. "I don't think they would guide (investors) to this type of earnings for the next quarter."
The company was not immediately available for comment on its second fiscal quarter ending in March.
((--Chicago Newsdesk (312) 408-8787))
